summary: Brief is clear on core CRUD and privacy, but the in-memory store contradicts the stated problem, and abuse/resource limits, identity validation and the risk register are incomplete.

criteria.description: Not met: no limits on request size, notes per user or memory; X-User format unspecified; no logging; no id scheme.
Not met: AC5 'clear message' and 'never causes a server error' are vague; no AC for oversized bodies, wrong types; check order of 401 vs 400/422 undefined.
Not met: A1 is unverifiable by the service and mitigated only by a README sentence.
Met: zero-dependency node:http plus repository interface is proportionate.
Not met: spoofable identity header, no body size cap, unbounded memory growth (DoS).
Met: no AI features; not applicable.
Not met: only two risks; no likelihood, impact or owner; DoS and gateway-misconfiguration spoofing not listed.

findings.title: In-memory store does not solve the stated problem
findings.detail: Problem says local files are 'lost between machines' and need an API; but RISK-2/Q1 accept data loss on every restart, so the product is not a reliable private notes place. Persistence is deferred with no date (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Problem, #Risks, #Open Questions).
findings.recommendation: Either add file/DB persistence behind the repository interface to scope, or explicitly redefine this release as a prototype/demo with a visible warning, and name an owner and decision date for Q1.

findings.title: No resource limits or abuse controls
findings.detail: Body is capped at 2000 chars by validation, but there is no HTTP request-size cap (node:http reads unbounded streams), no per-user note count cap, no rate limit. A2 says a few hundred notes but nothing enforces it; memory can be exhausted (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Acceptance Criteria, #Assumptions).
findings.recommendation: Add requirements and ACs: max request payload (413 above N KB), max notes per user with a defined error, and state rate limiting is gateway-owned. Add tests.

findings.title: Identity header handling underspecified
findings.detail: AC6 covers only a missing X-User. Empty, whitespace, overlong, odd-character values and repeated headers are unspecified; a value like '__proto__' could break a plain-object store. Safety relies solely on README text for A1 (RISK-1) (artifact:.eccode/artifacts/brief.md#Risks).
findings.recommendation: Define X-User validation (charset/length, 401 otherwise), require Map-based storage, add a test. Add a technical control for A1 (e.g. loopback/configurable bind host) beyond documentation.

findings.title: Validation and error contract gaps
findings.detail: AC5 does not define behaviour for non-string or missing title/body, non-object JSON, wrong content-type, unknown routes, wrong methods, invalid id format, or check order (401 before parse). 'Never causes a server error' needs a generic 500 policy that leaks nothing.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate these cases in AC5 with status codes; require a generic 500 body without stack traces, tested.

findings.title: Risk register incomplete
findings.detail: Risks lack likelihood, impact and owner; missing: header spoofing via gateway misconfiguration, memory exhaustion, id guessability.
findings.recommendation: Convert to a table with likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner and add the missing risks.

findings.title: Unspecified note schema, ids, ordering, logging
findings.detail: No id format, list ordering, timestamps, response shape for 'stored note', or logging policy is defined.
findings.recommendation: Specify note schema (UUID id, owner, title, body, createdAt), list ordering, and minimal request logging that excludes bodies.
